message: **The `AI proxy: cascade dispatch failed` log line names the credential's provider lock when it is why dispatch exhausted.** A cascade tier naming a provider the calling credential's `provider` allow/block policy excludes used to log a bare `cascade exhausted without dispatching any tier` before the client's generic `502`, naming neither the lock nor the requested provider. When that lock is the only reason no tier ever dispatched, the logged error now reads `cascade exhausted: every candidate tier was excluded by the credential's provider policy (allowed=..., blocked=...); routing plan requested provider(s) [...], which this credential cannot reach`. A cascade that also hit an unrelated cause (a cost cap, an unhealthy provider, a transport error) keeps the generic message, so the new detail is never misattributed. The HTTP response to the caller is unchanged; this is a server-side diagnostics improvement, not a new field in the `502` body.
